evidence.claim: Modi said the Ukraine-Russia conflict required an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy as the only way forward.
evidence.title: Visit of the Prime Minister of the United Kingdom to India (April 21-22, 2022)
evidence.excerpt: Modi said the Ukraine-Russia conflict required an immediate cessation of violence and a return to direct dialogue and diplomacy as the only way forward.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official bilateral statement on the PMO site, dated in the target year.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement during the target year.
contrary_evidence: Again, this is rhetorical restraint rather than a demonstrable nuclear-risk reduction measure.

evidence.claim: India said it was disturbed by developments in Ukraine, called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, emphasized the UN Charter and territorial integrity, and said dialogue was the only way to settle disputes before abstaining.
evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Draft Resolution on Ending Ukraine Crisis, as Russian Federation Wields Veto
evidence.excerpt: India said it was disturbed by developments in Ukraine, called for an immediate cessation of hostilities, emphasized the UN Charter and territorial integrity, and said dialogue was the only way to settle disputes before abstaining.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN meeting record with India's explicit explanation of vote.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Government position under Modi through India’s UN mission, not a direct personal statement.
contrary_evidence: India did not join the condemnation bloc or sanctions regime.

evidence.claim: India abstained on the draft resolution condemning the referenda and purported annexation of occupied Ukrainian territories.
evidence.title: Security Council Fails to Adopt Resolution Condemning Moscow's Referenda in Ukraine’s Occupied Territories, as Permanent Member Employs Veto
evidence.excerpt: India abstained on the draft resolution condemning the referenda and purported annexation of occupied Ukrainian territories.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous UN vote record naming India.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Reflects the government’s cautious multilateral stance under Modi.
contrary_evidence: The abstention preserved ties with Russia while limiting explicit alignment with the condemning bloc.

evidence.claim: Modi said the Ukraine crisis had created an energy and food crisis and urged stronger SCO cooperation, mutual trust, and full transit rights among members.
evidence.title: English Translation of Remarks by Prime Minister, Shri Narendra Modi at the SCO Summit
evidence.publisher: Press Information Bureau / Prime Minister's Office
evidence.excerpt: Modi said the Ukraine crisis had created an energy and food crisis and urged stronger SCO cooperation, mutual trust, and full transit rights among members.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary 2022 PMO translation of the Prime Minister’s remarks.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year and directly attributable to Modi.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler speech; it reflects Modi’s public diplomatic position.
contrary_evidence: The remarks are broad regional diplomacy, not proof of concrete conflict settlement.
They do not resolve the Russia-Ukraine war or border disputes by themselves.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that the United States urged India not to increase Russian oil purchases, while noting India had already bought at least 13 million barrels of Russian crude since the invasion and had not imposed sanctions on Russia.
evidence.title: Blinken urges Indian FM not to buy additional Russian oil
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that the United States urged India not to increase Russian oil purchases, while noting India had already bought at least 13 million barrels of Russian crude since the invasion and had not imposed sanctions on Russia.
evidence.source_locator: story text summary in the Reuters archive record
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Reuters reporting with a contemporaneous archival record and explicit sourcing from U.S. and Indian officials.
evidence.period_fit: Directly within the target year, shortly after the invasion.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Not a personal order from Modi, but a strong indicator of the government’s balancing between peace rhetoric and material ties to Russia.
contrary_evidence: Energy security can explain some of the trade, but it still weakened pressure on Moscow.
This does not show direct participation in the war, only limited restraint on ties with Russia.

unresolved_gaps: No public 2022 evidence of a Modi-directed command-and-control reform, custody audit, launch-readiness change, or internal NCA practice change.
Personal attribution is thin for the more favorable multilateral statements and nuclear-governance positions.
The Russia balancing record is mostly government-level and UN-mission level rather than a clearly documented personal decision by Modi on oil, abstentions, or summit sequencing.
There is no 2022 external-combat or proxy-war exposure to test civilian-protection or proxy-control lenses in a strong way.
Direct Modi-level incitement evidence is thinner than the broader BJP and state-level abuse record.
The strongest custody-death and abuse claims still rely on NGO and U.S. State Department reporting with mixed central/state attribution.
Direct evidence of Modi personally directing electoral manipulation is thin relative to the stronger party-level and institutional record.
Several items show contestability and oversight but do not themselves prove that Modi strengthened democratic institutions in 2022.
Household-level and median-welfare evidence is thinner than the macro, capex, and program-count evidence.
Corruption, favoritism, and politically connected business privilege are underdeveloped relative to investment and growth material.
Independent outcome measures and subnational equity checks are still thin relative to the many ministry self-reports.
The current record is strong on inputs and service counts but weak on durable quality, learning, nutrition, and sustained poverty improvement.
No audited evidence of direct personal falsehood, correction, or hidden conflicts of interest has been recovered for 2022.
The negative items are mostly institutional opacity or noncooperation, not direct proof of personal self-dealing or a documented lie by Modi.
Project-level outcome audits and durability checks are still thinner than the program-design and rollout material.
Direct evidence that Modi replaced a specific ineffective implementer is absent.
